Perform the following:

  • Prioritize scripts and assign start and end dates for test script execution; prioritization is based on script complexity and length of time for the script to complete
  • Calculate the total amount of time it should take to execute all test scenarios, resolve defects and re-execute
  • Review and adjust the number of resources as required to meet the allotted time to complete the test execution
  • Assign an owner responsible for achieving successful execution for each test script; assignment is a common practice to increase accountability in the test effort

Since test scripts often have specific data needs, availability of test data is also considered when scheduling test execution. Scheduling execution of some test scripts may require discussion of when test data become available, which may be dependent on what type of test data is being used and how it is created.

Another factor to consider while scheduling test execution is external dependencies that impact the test effort. Particularly with large projects, the test effort may rely on completed tasks from other parts of the project. These dependencies are discussed, documented and presented to stakeholders. For the duration of the test effort, external dependencies and other integration points are monitored, addressed and accounted for while scheduling the execution of test scripts.

In agile methodology, scheduling test execution is an ongoing effort and test scripts are assigned to a test cycle on a daily basis based on the available functionality. If there is a dependency between test scripts then they are assigned to a different test cycle.

The purpose of this task is to:

  • Coordinate execution of test scripts
  • Establish a baseline for tracking test execution progress
  • Assess test effort estimates and evaluate any impacts to project timelines
  • Verify that enough resources have been assigned to the test cycle so that it can be accomplished on time
